belief: Life is never stable or safe.
origins: Childhood in an unpredictable home, repeated moves, a frightening event, or growing up around constant financial strain can teach the mind that the ground is never solid. When hardship comes often, the nervous system learns to stay on guard, and it can begin to feel as if danger is always near.
teaches: Scripture does not promise a life without trouble. Jesus said that in the world we will have tribulation, but that we can take courage because He has overcome the world. God is called our refuge and an ever-present help in trouble. The Bible also invites us to lie down and sleep in peace because God makes us dwell in safety. These verses speak of a steadiness that rests on God, even when circumstances shake.
self_statements: Something bad is always about to happen.
Nothing in life can be counted on.
I have to stay on guard all the time.
Just when things settle down, they fall apart.
errors: Turning past instability into “life is always unsafe.”
Expecting trouble that has not come.
Feeling on edge and concluding that I am in danger.
Noticing threats while overlooking what is steady.
questions: What in my past taught me that life is unstable?
What, right now, is stable and safe?
Am I in danger at this moment, or is my body reacting to an old alarm?
What has God provided in past hard times?
What does it mean to find refuge in God, not in perfect circumstances?
What is one small routine I could build that adds stability?
Who could I talk with if I feel unsafe?
truth: Life has real uncertainty, and I cannot control everything. But “never stable or safe” is not the whole truth. There are steady things today, and God is my refuge and help in trouble. I can build small routines, trust Him for what I cannot control, and rest.
hw_truths: God is my refuge, even when life shakes.
Some things in my life are steady.
I can build small routines that give stability.
Feeling on edge does not prove I am in danger.
I have gotten through hard times before.
I can rest in God’s care tonight.
log: Each evening, write one thing that was stable or safe today and rate how safe you felt from 0 to 10.
actions: Choose a regular wake-up, meal, or evening routine and keep it for a week.
Name what is safe right now.
Look around and name five things that are safe in this moment. Breathe slowly while you do.
Share one fear about safety and notice how it feels to be heard.
Read Psalm 46:1–2 or Psalm 4:8 slowly each night this week.
prayer: Lord, You are my refuge and strength. When my life feels shaky, steady my heart. Help me find rest in Your care, build small steadiness into my days, and trust You with what I cannot control. Amen.
